nodes.label: Egyptian National Curriculum
Mathematics — Preparatory 3 (English)
Unit 1 — Relations and Functions
Algebra
Represent ordered pairs and decide when they are equal
nodes.description: Represent ordered pairs as points in the coordinate plane, and use equality of ordered pairs to find unknown values.

nodes.label: Find the Cartesian product of two finite sets
nodes.description: Find X×Y, Y×X and X² from the definition, compare them, and find the number of elements.

nodes.label: Represent a Cartesian product of finite sets by an arrow diagram and a Cartesian diagram
nodes.description: Draw an arrow diagram and a Cartesian diagram for X×Y and X×X.

nodes.label: Represent N×N, Z×Z and Q×Q in the coordinate plane and identify points
nodes.description: Draw the perpendicular net for infinite sets and read or plot the ordered pairs given by points.

nodes.label: Locate points of R×R by quadrant or axis and decide membership in X×X
nodes.description: Use the axes and quadrants of R×R to locate points, and decide whether points belong to X×X for an interval X.

nodes.label: Represent a relation from X to Y
nodes.description: Write a relation between two sets as ordered pairs and as an arrow diagram.

nodes.label: Write and represent a relation given by a rule
nodes.description: Find the ordered pairs of a relation defined by a rule and show it in an arrow diagram and a cartesian diagram.

nodes.label: Relate a relation to the cartesian product
nodes.description: Decide that a relation from X to Y is a subset of X × Y.

nodes.label: Represent a relation on a set itself
nodes.description: Write and represent a relation from a set to itself, R ⊂ X × X, with arrow and cartesian diagrams.

nodes.label: Decide whether a relation is a function
nodes.description: Decide whether a relation from X to Y is a function by checking that each element of X appears only once as a first projection, using arrow diagrams, cartesian diagrams and ordered pairs.

nodes.label: Represent a function symbolically
nodes.description: Write a function with symbols such as f : X → Y, f : x ↦ y and f(x) = y, and name the image of an element.

nodes.label: Represent a function by arrow and cartesian diagrams
nodes.description: Represent a function or relation by a set of ordered pairs, an arrow diagram and a cartesian diagram, and tell which diagrams show functions.

nodes.label: Find the domain, codomain and range of a function
nodes.description: Identify the domain, codomain and range of a function, and see that the range is a subset of the codomain.

nodes.label: Identify polynomial functions and state their degree
nodes.description: Decide whether a function rule is a polynomial and find its degree from the highest power of x.

nodes.label: Evaluate a polynomial function at given values
nodes.description: Find the image of a number under a polynomial function and combine function values.

nodes.label: Represent linear and constant functions graphically
nodes.description: Draw the graph of a linear or constant function as a straight line using a table of two or three ordered pairs.

nodes.label: Represent quadratic functions graphically
nodes.description: Draw the parabola of a quadratic function from a table of values over an interval.

nodes.label: Find the vertex, axis of symmetry and extreme value of a quadratic
nodes.description: Use the sign of a and the formula x = -b/2a to find the vertex, the opening direction, the axis of symmetry and the minimum or maximum value.

questions.stem: Find a set of the ordered pairs which satisfy the relation: $y = 2x - 1$ when $x = 0$ and $x = 1$, $x = 2$
solution: The ordered pairs are (0, -1), (1, 1), (2, 3)

questions.stem: Does the ordered pair $(3, 5)$ equal the ordered pair $(5, 3)$? (Use the graph).
solution: Plot (3, 5): go 3 along the x-axis, then 5 up.
Plot (5, 3): go 5 along the x-axis, then 3 up.
The two points are in different places.
Each ordered pair is represented by one and only one point.
Different points mean different pairs, since 3 ≠ 5 gives (3, 5) ≠ (5, 3).

questions.stem: Are the number of elements of $X\times Y$ = the number of elements of $Y\times X$?
solution: n(X × Y) = n(X) × n(Y)
n(Y × X) = n(Y) × n(X)
Multiplication does not depend on order, so the numbers are equal
Yes, they have the same number of elements even though the sets differ

solution: When $A=-1$: $\therefore B=2\times(-1)+4=2$

content.text_md: If $X=\{1, 2\}$, $Y\{3, 4, 5\}$ Find: $X\times Y$, and represent it:
The cartesian product of X × Y is represented by an arrow diagram, or a graphical net, as follows:
First: An arrow diagram. Draw an arrow from each element that represents the first projection (the elements of set X) to each element that represents the second projection (the elements of set Y).
i.e: the arrow diagram of the cartesian product represents each ordered pair by an arrow that starts from its first projection and ends at the second projection.

Second: Cartesian diagram (the perpendicular graphical net). On a perpendicular graph net, the elements of set X are represented horizontally and the elements of set Y vertically. The intersection points of the horizontal and vertical lines represent the ordered pairs of the elements of the cartesian product X × Y.
